cs.label: Prerekvizity:
cs.content: studentem studijního programu B-TPO Technologie potravin
Historický vývoj potravinářství – historické milníky konzumace a technologie zpracování potravin od pravěku po současnost. (dotace 2/0)
Potraviny a suroviny rostlinného původu a jejich zpracování – hlavní druhy potravinových surovin (obiloviny, luštěniny, okopaniny, olejniny aj.), základní metody zpracování. (dotace 2/0)
Potraviny a suroviny živočišného původu a jejich zpracování – hlavní druhy potravinových surovin (mléko, maso, vejce aj.), základní metody zpracování. (dotace 2/0)
Potraviny a suroviny ostatní a jejich zpracování – další druhy potravinových surovin (ovoce, zelenina, káva, čaj aj.), základní metody zpracování surovin. (dotace 2/0)
Potraviny a zdraví – vztahy mezi složením potravin, jejich zpracováním a nutriční hodnotou, alternativní způsoby výživy. (dotace 2/0)
Globální organizace v potravinářství – mezinárodní organizace a jejich role v potravinářském sektoru – FAO, WHO, Codex Alimentarius, WTO, GFSI, OIE a další iniciativy. (dotace 2/0)
Bezpečnost potravin a potravinářská legislativa EU a ČR – EU a české potravinové právo, organizace systému zajištění bezpečnosti potravin v EU a ČR – EFSA, SVS, SZPI, RASFF aj. (dotace 2/0)

Potravinová bezpečnost a soběstačnost – význam národní a globální produkce potravin, strategie států pro zvýšení potravinové soběstačnosti, hrozby pro potravinovou bezpečnost, vliv geopolitiky na dostupnost potravin. (dotace 2/0)

Umělá inteligence a digitální inovace v potravinářství – využití umělé inteligence a strojového učení v kvalitě, technologii a bezpečnosti potravin, blockchain pro sledování původu potravin, automatizace výroby aj. (dotace 2/0)

Výzkum, vývoj a inovace v potravinářském průmyslu – současné trendy a směry výzkumu v oblasti potravin (funkční potraviny, nutrigenomika, mikrobiom), využití 3D tisku potravin, inovativní obalové materiály, chytré obaly a senzory. (dotace 2/0)
Nové potraviny a alternativní zdroje potravin – potraviny na bázi hmyzu, fermentované potraviny, řasy, rostlinné alternativy živočišných produktů. (dotace 2/0)
Udržitelnost v potravinářství – strategie proti plýtvání potravinami, využití vedlejších surovin, prevence vzniku odpadů, upcyklace, snížení produkce obalů aj. (dotace 2/0)

en.label: Prerequisites:
en.content: student of study programme B-TPO Food Technology
Historical development of food processing – historical milestones in food consumption and processing technologies from prehistory to the present. (allowance 2/0)
Plant-based foods and raw materials and their processing – main types of plant-based food materials (cereals, legumes, root crops, oilseeds, etc.), basic processing methods. (allowance 2/0)
Animal-based foods and raw materials and their processing – main types of animal-based food materials (milk, meat, eggs, etc.), basic processing methods. (allowance 2/0)
Other foods and raw materials and their processing – additional types of food raw materials (fruits, vegetables, coffee, tea, etc.), basic methods of raw material processing. (allowance 2/0)
Food and health – relationships between food composition, processing, and nutritional value; alternative approaches to nutrition. (allowance 2/0)
Global organizations in the food sector – international organizations and their roles in the food sector – FAO, WHO, Codex Alimentarius, WTO, GFSI, OIE, and other initiatives. (allowance 2/0)

Food safety and food legislation in the EU and the Czech Republic – EU and Czech food law; structure of food safety systems in the EU and the Czech Republic – EFSA, SVA, CAFIA, RASFF, etc. (allowance 2/0)

Food security and self-sufficiency – the importance of national and global food production; state strategies for improving food self-sufficiency; threats to food security; impact of geopolitics on food availability. (allowance 2/0)

Artificial intelligence and digital innovations in the food industry – use of AI and machine learning in food quality, processing, and safety; blockchain for food traceability; production automation, etc. (allowance 2/0)

Research, development, and innovation in the food industry – current trends and research directions in food (functional foods, nutrigenomics, microbiome); use of 3D food printing; innovative packaging materials, smart packaging and sensors. (allowance 2/0)
Novel foods and alternative food sources – insect-based foods, fermented foods, algae, and plant-based alternatives to animal products. (allowance 2/0)
Sustainability in the food industry – strategies against food waste, use of by-products, waste prevention, upcycling, reduction of packaging materials, etc. (allowance 2/0)

en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The course introduces students to the fundamentals of food science, including plant and animal raw materials, processing technologies, nutrition, legislation, innovation, and sustainability. It fosters a broader understanding of food in the context of current global challenges.

(allowance 2/0)3.Animal-based foods and raw materials and their processing – main types of animal-based food materials (milk, meat, eggs, etc.), basic processing methods. (allowance 2/0)4.Other foods and raw materials and their processing – additional types of food raw materials (fruits, vegetables, coffee, tea, etc.), basic methods of raw material processing. (allowance 2/0)5.Food and health – relationships between food composition, processing, and nutritional value; alternative approaches to nutrition. (allowance 2/0)6.Global organizations in the food sector – international organizations and their roles in the food sector – FAO, WHO, Codex Alimentarius, WTO, GFSI, OIE, and other initiatives. (allowance 2/0)7.Food safety and food legislation in the EU and the Czech Republic – EU and Czech food law; structure of food safety systems in the EU and the Czech Republic – EFSA, SVA, CAFIA, RASFF, etc. (allowance 2/0)8.Food security and self-sufficiency – the importance of national and global food production; state strategies for improving food self-sufficiency; threats to food security; impact of geopolitics on food availability. (allowance 2/0)9.Artificial intelligence and digital innovations in the food industry – use of AI and machine learning in food quality, processing, and safety; blockchain for food traceability; production automation, etc. (allowance 2/0)10.Research, development, and innovation in the food industry – current trends and research directions in food (functional foods, nutrigenomics, microbiome); use of 3D food printing; innovative packaging materials, smart packaging and sensors. (allowance 2/0)11.Novel foods and alternative food sources – insect-based foods, fermented foods, algae, and plant-based alternatives to animal products. (allowance 2/0)12.Sustainability in the food industry – strategies against food waste, use of by-products, waste prevention, upcycling, reduction of packaging materials, etc. (allowance 2/0)
